name: Homeschool Haven
summary: A public website plus family, educator and admin portals for a homeschool community in Cape Coral, Florida.
challenge: Home School Haven's classes, calendar, contact and payment lived in separate places. The goal was one connected product: a public site families can browse, and private portals where parents register children, educators see only their own programs and administrators run enrollment.

decisions.title: Authorization in the database
decisions.detail: Supabase row-level security and least-privilege grants decide who sees what. One family cannot see another's records, and an educator sees only assigned programs. The boundary was checked by signing in as each sample role and probing the API directly.

decisions.title: Provisioned accounts only
decisions.detail: There is no self-service sign-up, and students never sign in; a parent manages each child. Sign-in failures read the same whether or not an account exists, and recovery links are verified on the server.

decisions.title: Honest checkout handoff
decisions.detail: Registration hands off to the organization's existing checkout page. Coming back from checkout never marks anything paid: a registration stays pending until an administrator confirms payment.

detail: The current build is a demo for the owner's review and runs on sample families and children. Real families are not invited until the owner confirms the policy checklist, and placeholder imagery is blocked from production builds.
role: Solo build: I engineered, built and set up this project.
